## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 2 â€” GameModel cluster review.

## Problem (P1)
`TaomSiegeEventModel.GetAvailableDefenderSiegeEngines` calls `party.MobileParty.HasPerk(...)` without a null guard. `MobileParty` returns `null` for garrison parties (settlements defended by their garrison alone, with no leader army present). This is the common defender shape in early-game sieges and unattached settlements.

- File: `Main/Features/Siege/Models/TaomSiegeEventModel.cs:23-24`

## Analysis
Vanilla `DefaultSiegeEventModel.GetAvailableDefenderSiegeEngines` accesses `party.LeaderHero` (not `party.MobileParty`) for perk checks â€” TAOM's restructured override changed the access path without adding the corresponding null guard. Per `adapters.md`: "TaleWorlds computed getters crash before your null check â€” use `?.`."

## Solution
Guard with `?.` and short-circuit safely:
```csharp
bool hasFirePerks = party.MobileParty?.HasPerk(DefaultPerks.Engineering.SiegeWorks) == true
                 || party.MobileParty?.HasPerk(DefaultPerks.Engineering.Counterweights) == true;
```

## Files
- `Main/Features/Siege/Models/TaomSiegeEventModel.cs` (override body)
- `TAOM.Tests/Features/Siege/` (add regression test exercising garrison-defender shape)

## Testing
Unit test: `GetAvailableDefenderSiegeEngines_GarrisonDefenderNullMobileParty_NoNREFallsBackToVanilla`. Add a fake `PartyBase` with `MobileParty == null`.

## Phase reference
Phase 2 cluster review â€” `docs/audits/cluster-gamemodels.md` master findings row 1 + Siege per-feature section.

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 2 â€” GameModel cluster review.

## Problem (P1)
`TaomPartySpeedModel.CalculateFinalSpeed` accesses `Campaign.Current.MapSceneWrapper.GetFaceTerrainType(...)` without any null guards on the chain. `Campaign.Current` is null before campaign load; `MapSceneWrapper` can be null during scene transitions and on early loading-screen ticks. `CalculateFinalSpeed` is called every tick per party â€” high-frequency hot path.

- File: `Main/Features/CulturalFeats/Models/TaomPartySpeedModel.cs:30`

## Analysis
The override was added to apply Rohan/forest culture speed feats based on terrain type. The chain `Campaign.Current.MapSceneWrapper.GetFaceTerrainType(...)` is two layers of unguarded computed property access. Per `adapters.md` and `csharp-architecture.md` rule "?. for computed TaleWorlds properties".

Secondary issue at lines 47-61: a `foreach` over the full troop roster with a `mountedCount` accumulator runs on every tick per party with no early-exit when culture mismatch is known.

## Solution
1. Guard the terrain access:
```csharp
var terrain = Campaign.Current?.MapSceneWrapper?.GetFaceTerrainType(mobileParty.CurrentNavigationFace)
            ?? TerrainType.Plain;
```
2. Add an early-exit before the roster walk when the party's culture is not Rohan (the only culture that consumes the mounted-ratio):
```csharp
if (mobileParty.Party?.Culture?.StringId != "rohan_culture_id") return finalSpeed;
```
3. As part of Pattern A service-extraction, move the `foreach` into `ICulturalFeatsService.ApplyPartySpeedFeats(...)`.

## Files
- `Main/Features/CulturalFeats/Models/TaomPartySpeedModel.cs`
- `TAOM.Tests/Features/CulturalFeats/` (add `TaomPartySpeedModelTests.cs` once extracted to service)

## Testing
Unit test the extracted service with: (a) `Campaign.Current == null`, (b) `MapSceneWrapper == null`, (c) Rohan culture + mounted roster, (d) non-Rohan culture (skip roster walk).

## Phase reference
Phase 2 cluster review â€” `docs/audits/cluster-gamemodels.md` master findings row 1b + CulturalFeats per-feature section.

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 3 â€” CampaignBehavior cluster review.

## Findings

### P1 â€” `Gold` (int) and `Influence` (float) parsed without range/NaN validation; asymmetric with PlayerGold
- File: `Main/Features/StartupResources/StartupResourcesConfigProvider.cs:54-55`
- `PlayerGold` goes through `ParsePlayerGold` which validates range `[0, 10_000_000]`. `Gold` and `Influence` use bare `int.Parse`/`float.Parse`:
  - `gold="-500000"` passes int.Parse â†’ flows to `_goldGiftAdapter.GiveGoldToHero(heroId, -500000)`.
  - `influence="NaN"` returns NaN; the downstream guard `entry.Influence > 0f` evaluates false silently â€” no warning logged. Per csharp-architecture.md "NaN BEFORE the range check", this violates the rule.
  - `gold="abc"` causes int.Parse throw â†’ caught by outer catch â†’ discards ENTIRE config (all entries lost).
- R3 pattern. Memory: `csharp-architecture.md` "Config Providers MUST Validate" â€” bug class has shipped 3Ã—.
- Fix: extract `ParseGold(string raw, string cultureId)` and `ParseInfluence` mirroring `ParsePlayerGold`. `FiniteFloatValidator` for influence. Range check `[0, max]` for gold.

### P2 â€” `_goldDistributed` / `_influenceDistributed` are dead guards (Simplicity Criterion violation)
- File: `Main/Features/StartupResources/StartupResourcesBehavior.cs:12-13,30-46`
- The `if (index != 1) return;` guard at line 30 already ensures the event handler body fires at most once per new-game flow. The `_goldDistributed` / `_influenceDistributed` guards at 32 + 46 can only fire if the engine delivers `index == 1` twice (engine invariant violation, not our concern).
- Booleans aren't in SyncData and don't protect across sessions either. They create misleading appearance of idempotency without actually protecting anything.
- Per `simplicity-criterion.md`: tiny win + added complexity + no real protection = Reject.
- Fix: remove `_goldDistributed`, `_influenceDistributed`, both if-guards. Retain only the index check + direct service calls.

### P3 â€” `OnNewGameCreatedPartialFollowUpEvent` at `index == 1` initialization-order concern
- File: `Main/Features/StartupResources/StartupResourcesBehavior.cs:24-26`
- If `GetAliveLordHeroes()` / `GetEligibleClans()` are backed by `Campaign.Current.Heroes`/`Campaign.Current.Clans` before those collections are fully populated by other behaviors at index 0, distribution silently skips lords.
- Fix: research via `ilspycmd` on SandBox; verify `index == 1` is correct slot.

## Recurring pattern
R3 (config validation gap) + Simplicity Criterion violation (aspirational dead guards).

## Test plan
- Unit: NaN influence rejected with warning log.
- Unit: negative gold rejected/clamped.
- Unit: malformed entry doesn't lose other entries.
- Verify Simplicity-Criterion fix preserves behavior (single grant per new-game).

## Phase reference
Phase 3 cluster review â€” `docs/audits/cluster-campaign-behaviors.md` "StartupResources" section.

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 3 â€” CampaignBehavior cluster review.

## Findings

### P1 â€” `SaveableTypeDefiner` registers `Dictionary<string,int>`, `Dictionary<int,int>`, `List<string>` â€” almost certainly collides with vanilla SandBox
- File: `Main/Features/CompanionTactics/FormationPresets/Models/FormationPresetSaveableTypeDefiner.cs:27-30`
- Generic container types are registered globally across all `SaveableTypeDefiner` instances. Vanilla SandBox almost certainly pre-registers `List<string>` and `Dictionary<string,int>` for vanilla lord/troop/equipment data. The TaleWorlds save system either throws on duplicate or silently uses first-registered.
- The catch-block in `SyncData` swallows exceptions silently â†’ presets reset to empty without player-facing notification. Player loses presets every load with no visible cause.
- CareerSystem deliberately avoided `SaveableTypeDefiner` for this reason (comment at `CareerPersistenceBehavior.cs:27`).
- Fix: switch to primitive-dict SyncData like CareerSystem â€” store `HoNFormationPreset` as flat dictionaries with primitive keys, eliminating the SaveableTypeDefiner.
- Verify: `ilspycmd "TaleWorlds.SaveSystem.dll" -t SaveableTypeDefiner` to enumerate vanilla container registrations.

### P1 â€” `SyncData` catch block silently resets presets to empty without player-facing notification
- File: `Main/Features/CompanionTactics/FormationPresets/Hooks/FormationPresetCampaignBehavior.cs:58-64`
- `LogWarning` to TAOM internal log only. Player won't see logs. They'll just lose presets repeatedly with no idea why.
- Fix: add `InformationManager.DisplayMessage(new InformationMessage("[CompanionTactics] Formation presets could not be loaded â€” reset to empty."))` inside catch block after LogWarning.

### P2 â€” `OnNewGameCreated` calls `_service.OnGameLoaded(empty list)` for reset (semantic mismatch)
- File: `Main/Features/CompanionTactics/FormationPresets/Hooks/FormationPresetCampaignBehavior.cs:73`
- `OnGameLoaded` is named for load-path use; reusing for new-game reset is an abstraction leak. Future load-path validation logic would inadvertently run on new-game.
- Fix: add `void Reset()` to `IFormationPresetService`; call instead of `OnGameLoaded(empty)`.

### P3 (out of scope) â€” `_heroFormationAssignments` doesn't prune dead heroes on load (delegate to OOBOverlayService review).
### P3 â€” `BaseId 726900601` collision risk if original developer's mod is also installed (cross-mod concern).

## Recurring pattern
R2 (silent SyncData failure â†’ state reset).

## Test plan
- Unit: simulate SaveableTypeDefiner collision; assert player sees in-game message.
- Verify: switch to primitive dict pattern; round-trip persistence test.

## Phase reference
Phase 3 cluster review â€” `docs/audits/cluster-campaign-behaviors.md` "CompanionTactics" section.

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 3 â€” CampaignBehavior cluster review.

## Verdict
**Inventory mutation pattern is correct.** Verified using `InventoryLogic.TransferCommand` + `AddTransferCommands` per memory `feedback_inventory_mutations_via_vanilla_inventorylogic.md`. Codex review #5 finding addressed; modifier preservation works; `SlotApplyOutcome.SlotLocked` confirmed removed.

## Findings

### P1 â€” `Patch33_SPInventoryVMRefresh` does silent-null concrete cast on adapter resolution
- File: `Main/Features/EquipPresets/Hooks/Patch33_SPInventoryVMRefresh.cs:37`
- `IoC.Resolve<IInventoryScreenAdapter>() as InventoryScreenAdapter` â€” concrete cast, succeeds today because IoC registers the same concrete class. If a future mock/alternative impl is registered, cast returns null and `SetActive` silently never fires; user-visible symptom is "presets overlay opens but shows no hero, can't load" with no log.
- Root cause: `SetActive` is a method on `InventoryScreenAdapter` but NOT on `IInventoryScreenAdapter` â€” the interface seam is missing.
- Fix: expose `void SetActive(SPInventoryVM? vm)` on `IInventoryScreenAdapter`; remove the concrete cast; add `_cachedLogger?.LogWarning` branch when resolved adapter is null.

### P2 â€” `equipped` counter overcounts no-ops (already-equipped slots) in load path
- File: `Main/Adapters/InventoryScreenAdapter.cs:147-153`
- When a slot already holds the exact same `EquipmentElement` (item + modifier match), code does `equipped++` and `continue` â€” counted as successful equip. Feeds `PresetLoadResult.EquippedCount` exposed to player as "N items applied." Player sees "8 items applied" with no transfer commands issued â€” misleading.
- Same pattern as Codex #34 `feedback_user_facing_promise_must_match_code.md`.
- Fix: rename no-op branch count to `alreadyEquipped` (tracked separately); distinguish in `PresetLoadResult` or VM surface.

### P3 â€” Doc rot in `docs/features/equip-presets.md:88` references removed `SlotApplyOutcome` enum.
### P3 â€” Doc rot in `docs/features/equip-presets.md:93` describes removed direct-mutation write path.

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 3 â€” CampaignBehavior cluster review.

## Verdict
**GameState pattern is correct.** Verified `manager.CreateState<FiefManagementGameState>() + PushState` â€” Codex #36 fix in place. `IGameStateListener` implemented (`feedback_gamestate_listener.md` mandate satisfied).

## Findings

### P1 â€” `RemoteFiefSettlementSwapper.Restore` silently bails when `MobileParty.MainParty` is null at OnFinalize
- File: `Main/Adapters/RemoteFiefSettlementSwapper.cs:42-47`
- `Restore` reads `MobileParty.MainParty` at restore-time and silently returns if null. If null at `OnFinalize` time (campaign ending from screen, exception in `TownManagementVM.ExecuteDone()` triggering state reset before finalization), swap is never restored.
- Global `MobileParty._currentSettlement` left pointing at remote fief â†’ corrupts party movement, AI, all subsequent F6 invocations in the same session.
- The `_swapActive` flag in `GauntletFiefManagementScreen.OnFinalize` correctly gates Restore call but Restore itself can still no-op.
- Fix: hold `_party` ref captured at `Swap` time (instance field); use captured ref in `Restore` rather than re-querying. Also: `LogError` on null-party at restore (signals corruption has occurred).

### P2 â€” `FiefHubMenuPresenter` Singleton has 4 stateful fields; `Reset()` only resets `_selectedIndex`
- File: `Main/Features/FiefManagement/FiefHubMenuPresenter.cs:15-17,32`
- Other 3 fields (`_menuFiefs`, `_menuCurrentFief`, `_menuCurrentAtPlayer`) NOT cleared. New campaign 2 in same process: `_menuFiefs` contains stale `FiefSummary` objects from prior campaign. `ManageOptionEnabled` returns true with stale `_menuCurrentFief`. `_menuFiefs.Count > 1` makes Prev/Next options visible with stale data before first `Refresh()`.
- R1 pattern.
- Fix: in `Reset()`, also assign `_menuFiefs = System.Array.Empty<FiefSummary>(); _menuCurrentFief = null; _menuCurrentAtPlayer = false;`.

### P2 â€” `FiefHubService.Count` triggers full `Settlement.All` iteration (862 settlements) on every F6 press
- File: `Main/Features/FiefManagement/FiefHubService.cs:37-59` + `Patch36_MapScreenF6:55`
- `GetOrderedFiefs()` iterates `Settlement.All` per call; `Count`, `Clamp`, `Next`, `Previous` all call it. `Patch36_MapScreenF6` calls `service.Count` on every F6 press. Bounded but unnecessary.
- Fix: presenter-cached `Count` (already cached after `Refresh()`), OR fast-path `Clan.PlayerClan?.Settlements.Count(s => s.IsTown || s.IsCastle)` without constructing summaries.

### P3 â€” `FiefManagementGameState.Fief` exposes sealed `Settlement` (ADR-007). Mitigated by terminating at UI boundary, but makes the model untestable.
- Fix: store `string SettlementId` instead; resolve at screen-open via adapter.

### P3 â€” `IGameStateListener` empty stubs (acceptable given `IsMenuState=true`).

TAOM feature audit Phase 2 â€” GameModel cluster review.

## Findings (7 Ã— P2)
Construction integrity: âœ… all 16 ctors match SubModule.cs:276â€“292. 15 are no-arg; `TaomSettlementLoyaltyModel(IRevoltTuningConfigProvider)` at line 288 matches its 1-arg ctor. **No P1 silent service drops** â€” the audit's primary suspicion is cleared.

### P2 â€” Systemic rule-4 violation across all 16 models (umbrella)
- Files: every `Main/Features/CulturalFeats/Models/Taom*Model.cs`
- All 16 override bodies contain `if`-branching, multi-line computation, or `foreach` logic. No `ICulturalFeatsService` exists; feat-dispatch is inlined everywhere. Per-model line ranges in cluster doc.
- 8 of the 16 also call `CareerPassiveHelper.ApplyFactor` directly inside the body (cross-feature coupling â€” Pattern D, separate issue).
- Fix: introduce `ICulturalFeatsService` (or per-domain `IXxxFeatsService`); model bodies become 1-line delegate + base fallback.

### P2 â€” TaomCaravanModel uses `CharacterObject.PlayerCharacter` static â€” feat silently player-only
- File: `TaomCaravanModel.cs:13`
- `GetCaravanFormingCost` is called for AI caravans too; the Umbar Corsair-Trade feat description implies faction-wide reduction but only the player benefits. Semantic bug + ADR-007 violation.

### P2 â€” TaomBattleRewardModel asymmetric coalesce
- File: `TaomBattleRewardModel.cs:25`
- Feat path uses `party.Owner?.Culture ?? party.Culture`; career path uses `party.Owner ?? party.LeaderHero`. The two paths can disagree on party "owner" â†’ feat applies, career skips (or vice versa) for the same combat event.

### P2 â€” TaomClanFinanceModel defensive `?.` on non-nullable parameter
- File: `TaomClanFinanceModel.cs:19`
- `clan?.Culture` uses `?.` on a parameter typed non-nullable `Clan`. Silently skips feat instead of surfacing invariant violation. Suggests defensive paranoia rather than knowing the input contract.

### P2 â€” TaomSettlementProsperityModel compound condition is a business rule
- File: `TaomSettlementProsperityModel.cs:22,25,28`
- `if (feat-check && result.ResultNumber >= 0f)` is a business rule (apply-only-if-growing), not a guard. Belongs in service.

### P2 â€” TaomSmithingModel logic extracted to private static method on model
- File: `TaomSmithingModel.cs:29â€“56`
- `ApplySmithingFeatReduction` (28 lines) lives on the model class â€” rule 4 requires extraction to a Service, not to a method on the model.
- Fix: move into `ISmithingFeatsService` (or shared `ICulturalFeatsService`); inject via constructor.

### P2 â€” TaomPartySpeedModel roster `foreach` on per-tick hot path
- File: `TaomPartySpeedModel.cs:47â€“61`

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 3 â€” CampaignBehavior cluster review.

## Verdict
**Wiring is clean.** SyncData key, apply path (Patch34 Postfix), and singleton lifetime all correct. The bugs are semantic â€” the implementation contradicts CLAUDE.md's stated "per-save toggle" contract.

## Findings

### P2 â€” `OnGameLoaded` reconciler unconditionally overwrites saved `_isSearchAvailable` with current MCM value
- File: `Main/Features/QuickActions/Hooks/InventorySearchCampaignBehavior.cs:51-56`
- CLAUDE.md key paths table promises "per-save `IsSearchAvailable` toggle via `InventorySearchCampaignBehavior` SyncData + Postfix on `SPInventoryVM.RefreshCallbacks`."
- Implementation: `OnGameLoaded` writes `_isSearchAvailable = _settings.EnableInventorySearch` whenever they differ. Per-save intent is silently lost on every load. SyncData becomes a one-frame cache rather than durable per-save state.
- Fix (option A â€” keep per-save semantics): remove `OnGameLoaded` handler entirely. SyncData restores from save before any events fire; the only legitimate concern (upgrade from key-less save) requires a version sentinel which doesn't exist.
- Fix (option B â€” embrace MCM-wins semantics): remove SyncData entirely; read MCM directly in the Postfix; update CLAUDE.md to say "global MCM toggle" not "per-save toggle".
- **Pick one approach. The current code does both at once and corrupts the contract.**

### P2 â€” `OnTick` reconciler also overwrites per-save state on every campaign frame after MCM change
- File: `Main/Features/QuickActions/Hooks/InventorySearchCampaignBehavior.cs:66-67`
- Same root issue as above. Combined with `OnGameLoaded`, the SyncData value at save time will always equal the current MCM value â€” the per-save key is permanently redundant.
- Fix: same as P2 above (one approach, applied consistently).

### P3 â€” `Patch34_SPInventoryVMCapture` and `Patch34_SPInventoryVMFinalize` use concrete cast on adapter
- File: `Patch34_SPInventoryVMCapture.cs:27` + `Patch34_SPInventoryVMFinalize.cs:28`
- `IoC.Resolve<IInventoryVMAdapter>() as InventoryVMAdapter` â€” same pattern as EquipPresets P1. Silent null on resolution failure.
- Fix: add `SetActive`/`ClearActiveIfMatches` to `IInventoryVMAdapter` interface; drop concrete cast.

## Entity State Matrix
N/A. Behavior touches no Hero/Settlement/Clan/Party state. UI hint only.

## Recurring pattern
R2 (SyncData semantics broken by load-path overwrite â€” same shape as Diplomacy `WarOfTheRingService.CurrentPhase`).

## Decision needed (from user)
Confirm whether "per-save toggle independent of MCM" is a hard requirement vs "MCM is always authoritative." The fix path is different for each.

## Test plan (depending on chosen semantics)
- Per-save: load save A (search ON) with MCM OFF â†’ verify search ON.
- MCM-wins: same scenario â†’ verify search OFF; document the reversal in CLAUDE.md.

## Phase reference
Phase 3 cluster review â€” `docs/audits/cluster-campaign-behaviors.md` "QuickActions" section.

## Source
TAOM feature audit Phase 2 â€” GameModel cluster review.

## Findings (3 Ã— P2)
Construction integrity: âœ… ctor `(IOnExecutionAction)` matches SubModule.cs:273 â€” but the choice of injecting a HOOK interface into a MODEL is itself a P2 architectural smell.

### P2 â€” `IOnExecutionAction` (hook interface) injected into a GameModel
- File: `Main/Features/Execution/Models/TaomExecutionRelationModel.cs:11` + `SubModule.cs:272â€“273`
- Hook interfaces are typically resolved via `IoC.ResolveAll<IOnX>()` in Harmony patches, not injected into models. No other model in TAOM's registry uses this pattern.
- Fix: introduce `IExecutionRelationService` wrapping `GetRelationModifier`; register `Reuse.Singleton`; inject into model. `ExecutionActionHook` can implement both `IOnExecutionAction` and `IExecutionRelationService`, or the service can be a separate thin wrapper over `IAlignmentService`.

### P2 â€” Override body has null-guard `if` + delegate call + `showQuickNotification = false` mutation (rule 4)
- File: `TaomExecutionRelationModel.cs:16â€“33`
- The `showQuickNotification` `out` mutation when `modified == 0` is logic, not a boundary conversion.
- Fix: hook returns a struct `(int RelationDelta, bool ShowNotification)`; model passes both back without inline branching.

### P2 â€” Direct `Hero.MainHero.MapFaction.StringId` access (ADR-007 violation)
- File: `TaomExecutionRelationModel.cs:20`
- Sealed TaleWorlds type accessed directly inside model body. Per ADR-007, sealed types should not cross the model boundary.
- Fix: pass the executor kingdom ID into the service call; resolve at the hook level via an `IPlayerContextAdapter`.
